findings.description: check() adds the refill to bucket.tokens on every call, but updated_at is only advanced on the allowed path. When a request is denied, the refilled tokens are kept and updated_at stays old. The next call computes elapsed from that old timestamp and adds the same interval's refill again. Example: capacity 10, rate 1/s, empty bucket at t=0. A denied call at t=5 leaves tokens=5. At t=6 the bucket should hold 6 tokens, but it computes 5+6 and caps at 10. Clients that keep retrying while limited therefore get a full bucket back far sooner than the configured rate, so the limit is exceeded.
findings.suggestion: Set bucket.updated_at = now right after applying the refill (line 69), before the allow/deny decision, so each interval is credited only once.
findings.title: Token refill is double-counted after a denied request
